priorStories.headline: Three states carry out executions in one day
priorStories.body:
Florida, Alabama and Indiana each carried out a lethal-injection execution Thursday.

Florida executed Jesse Guardado for the 2004 murder of Jackie Malone. Alabama executed Michael Taylor for killing Ivan and Lucille Moore in 1991. Indiana executed Jeffrey Weisheit shortly after midnight for killing two children in a 2010 house fire.

Guardado’s death was Florida’s 19th execution this year, tying the state’s annual record.

priorStories.headline: S&P 500 falls 4.4% in AI-led sell-off
priorStories.body:
The S&P 500 fell 4.4% Thursday, its largest one-day decline since April 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,833 points, or 3.4%, and the Nasdaq fell 5.5%.

Companies associated with artificial-intelligence data centers led the sell-off, which erased the previous day’s gains. The Nasdaq ended in correction territory relative to its October high.

candidates.summary: Japan’s Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi each closed 6% lower Friday as the previous day’s AI-led Wall Street sell-off spread globally. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.3%, mainland China’s Shanghai Composite lost 1.1%, and major European indexes opened lower.
candidates.title: AI-led market sell-off spreads to Asia and Europe

candidates.summary: Myanmar’s Union Election Commission announced that special elections will be held April 4, 2027, to fill vacancies in 55 constituencies. The vote will include areas where armed conflicts continue and towns recently recaptured by the military.
candidates.title: Myanmar schedules April parliamentary by-elections

candidates.summary: Interim results from South Africa’s local elections showed the African National Congress headed for a substantial decline in support and possible loss of control in major cities. The MK Party, founded by former president Jacob Zuma, was leading in the eThekwini municipality, which includes Durban, as counting continued.
candidates.title: South Africa election count points to major ANC losses

candidates.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, above the prior 12-month monthly average of 48,000, while the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier. Payroll estimates for August and September were revised upward by a combined 84,000 jobs.
candidates.title: US adds 165,000 jobs in October

candidates.summary: AI-related shares rebounded in U.S. morning trading after a two-day global sell-off. At 10:45 a.m. Eastern, the S&P 500 was up 0.8% and the Nasdaq was up 1.4%, with Nvidia gaining 4.1%. The rebound followed declines of about 6% in both Tokyo and Seoul and a 2.1% fall in Germany’s DAX.
candidates.title: US AI stocks rebound after global sell-off

candidates.summary: The United States, Australia, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and New Zealand jointly condemned Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong’s 10-year national-security sentence. The governments called for an end to prosecutions they described as unjust; Hong Kong and mainland Chinese officials rejected the criticism.
candidates.title: Ten governments condemn Joshua Wong prison sentence

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump and Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, discussed international efforts to de-escalate tensions involving Iran. Qatar’s media office said the emir urged continued dialogue, diplomatic resolution of disputes, protection of maritime navigation and security of energy supplies.
candidates.title: Trump and Qatar emir discuss Iran de-escalation

candidates.title: AI shares rebound as US markets finish mixed

candidates.summary: Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Prosecutors subsequently ordered the arrests of Peña and former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo in an investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses connected to the bank’s failure.
candidates.title: Paraguay Senate removes Peña as prosecutors order arrest

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff following Republicans’ midterm-election losses. Trump said Wiles would continue working for his political organization.
candidates.title: Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff

candidates.summary: China confirmed that discussions were underway about a possible meeting among Chinese leader Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Beijing’s confirmation did not establish that a summit had been scheduled.
candidates.title: China confirms discussions about Xi-Trump-Putin meeting

candidates.summary: Iran was reviewing proposals from Qatar intended to address differences with the United States over Tehran’s nuclear program, according to two Middle Eastern government officials. The reported development raised the possibility of renewed indirect negotiations, but no talks or agreement had been announced.
candidates.title: Iran reviews Qatari nuclear proposals

candidates.summary: Two Justice Department officials resigned, including the top federal prosecutor in Miami who had overseen an investigation targeting opponents of President Donald Trump. The departures followed Democrats’ gains in the midterm elections.
candidates.title: Two Justice Department officials resign

candidates.summary: Democrats secured control of both chambers of Arizona’s Legislature while retaining the governorship, producing the party’s first state-government trifecta there since 1966. The result was confirmed as additional races from Tuesday’s election were called.
candidates.title: Democrats secure Arizona governing trifecta

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay to begin a 12-day tour also covering Argentina and Peru, three weeks after surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. The Vatican estimated that about 30,000 people attended his arrival events in Montevideo.
candidates.title: Pope Leo begins South American tour after lung surgery
